At the heart of a bicycle’s gear-shifting mechanism is the derailleur, a mechanical device that moves the chain laterally across a series of sprockets to change the gear ratio. When the rider operates the shifters on the handlebars, they pull or release cable tension, which is transmitted through housing to the derailleur’s pivot points. This tension change causes the derailleur cage to move either inward or outward, physically guiding the chain from one cog to another. The precision of this movement is critical, as it ensures the chain engages smoothly with the new sprocket without skipping or falling off.
